brief: A base with a bay bin in one half of its cell.

requirements.requirement: A bay bin that fills one half of its position
requirements.evidence: bay:0#1,-1#bay3 is a hex-bin-bay-n-half-solid (half bay tray). It stands in the empty position at (1,-1,0) and fills half of it. check_build found no rule errors and the mesh check came back clear.

A bay can't fit on a single base. It stands in an empty spot and has to bolt to three bases that touch each other; with one base the configurator offered no place for it. So I added piece:1,0,0;full and piece:0,-1,0;full next to the original piece:0,0,0;full. The tray sits beside these bases, not inside a base's own cell.

finish.summary: I placed a half bay tray (hex-bin-bay-n-half-solid) in the empty spot at (1,-1,0). It needed two more bases: a bay tray can't attach to just one base and has to bolt to three that touch each other. With your single base the configurator offered nowhere to put it, so I added bases at (1,0,0) and (0,-1,0) beside the original at (0,0,0). The build now has 3 bases and 1 bay tray. The configurator checks found no errors, and the mesh check is clear. If you meant a half tray inside one base's own cell, that's a different part (a normal half bin), not a bay.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
